transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I’m here because I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. At work, one saw starts up, or somebody walks past the office, or I think about some other job I need to do, and I’m pulled away from whatever I was doing. Then I lose track, and before I know it the whole day’s gotten away from me.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down or not enjoying things. I haven’t really noticed that.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, more than you used to?
Not really, no. I mean, I worry some like anyone does, but I haven’t noticed myself worrying a lot more than usual or about everything.
Have you been feeling restless, fidgety, or unable to sit still for long periods?

Yeah, I do. If I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or sit through a long meeting, I get this wound-up feeling inside, like I need to get up and move around. Even though I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish, it’s hard.
Do you often find yourself acting without thinking, like interrupting others, blurting out answers, or feeling like you have to do things right now without waiting?

I’m not sure I’d say that’s a big thing for me. I don’t usually blurt things out or cut people off on purpose. Sometimes I might feel impatient, but I haven’t really noticed myself acting without thinking like that.
Do you also have trouble focusing on things at home, like when you're reading, watching TV, or talking with family, or is this mainly a problem at work?

It’s not just work, but work is where it really shows. I can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. One saw starts up, or somebody walks past the office, or I suddenly think about another job, and I’m off track. Then I look up and the whole day’s gotten away from me.
Do you also have trouble focusing on things at home, like when you're reading, watching TV, or talking with family, or is this mainly a problem at work?

It’s mainly the same thing I was saying — what really brings me in is I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. At work, if a saw starts up or someone walks past the office, or even if I just think of another job I need to do, I’m pulled off what I was doing. Then I try to get back to it and realize the whole day’s gotten away from me.
Do you also have trouble staying focused at home, like when you're reading, watching TV, or talking with family, or is it mostly just a problem at work?

It’s not only at work, but that’s where it hits me the hardest. I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. A saw starts up, someone walks by the office, or I think of another job I need to do, and I’m pulled off what I was doing. Then I try to get back to it and realize the whole day’s gotten away from me.
Can you think of a time when you were trying to focus at home or in a social setting, like having a conversation or reading, and the same kind of distraction happened to you?

Yeah, I mean at home it happens too. If I’m trying to read something, my mind just slips off of it. Or if I’m talking with somebody, some little noise or just a thought about something else I need to do pulls me away, and then I realize I haven’t really been following. It’s the same kind of thing — I just can’t keep my mind on one thing like I used to.
When did you first start noticing these problems with distraction and difficulty focusing — was it something that started when you were a child, or did it come on more recently as an adult?

It goes way back, honestly. I remember in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my mother I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, forget what I was supposed to do, or just sit there staring out the window instead of finishing my work. So it’s not brand-new, but it feels worse now.
Back when you were in grade school, did you have trouble finishing tasks, staying focused, or remembering things you were supposed to do?

Yes. Even back in grade school, before I was 12, I had trouble with that. Teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but careless. I’d lose homework, forget what they’d just told me to do, or just sit there staring out the window instead of finishing my work.
As a child, did you often have trouble staying seated, feel restless, or act without thinking before something was finished?

I don’t remember being the kid who couldn’t stay in her seat all the time, but the restless feeling, yeah. Even now, if I have to sit at a desk doing estimates or sit through a long meeting, I feel wound up inside, like I need to get up and move around. I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish, but it’s hard.
Have these difficulties with focus and restlessness caused problems in your life, like affecting your job performance, relationships, or ability to complete important tasks?

Yes, definitely. At work it’s caused real problems. I’ve made mistakes on measurements or ordering, and then we have to redo things. I’ve been late getting estimates or schedules done, and that’s cost me commissions. The crew doesn’t really trust me as much with scheduling or ordering anymore.

At home, my husband has taken over the bills and a lot of the reminders, because I keep misplacing papers or missing what needs to be done. It’s embarrassing, but it’s gotten to where I can’t really keep up with it on my own.
